column3: On gathering, the alleged objects of worship become enemies and deny that worship, directly matching the focus's disavowal.
Guidance on restrained speech does not clarify failed intercession or partners' disavowal.
The associators deny having associated at judgment, a related but different form of repudiation.
It challenges the claimants to produce their alleged partners, exposing the unsupported partnership claim.
The immediately preceding Hour scene establishes the despair of the guilty before the focus specifies its cause.
Alleged partners neither answer invocation nor remain loyal on the Day; they deny the association itself.
It directly states that intercessors' intercession will not benefit them.
The immediate continuation gives the punished outcome for those who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter.
The rhetorical denial of another god reinforces the invalidity of assigning partners, without the Day-of-judgment outcome.
The condemned explicitly report having no intercessors.
Its contrast between God and what they associate supports monotheism generally but not failed advocacy.
It identifies association as grave wrongdoing, supplying the core offense behind the focus's final disavowal.
The unequal allocation to alleged partners exposes the false partnership arrangement that later collapses.
The immediate next verse states that, on that Day, the parties will be separated.
It directly records the claim that powerless objects are intercessors with God and rejects its basis.
God's incomparability rules out any equal partner, though it does not address intercession.
The nearby command not to be among associators supplies the practical opposite of the focus's condemned position.
After loss, the man regrets having associated anyone with his Lord, a related recognition of false reliance.
It explains that intercession carries a share of its consequence, but not the focus's invalid intercession.
The torment scene does not clarify partners or intercession.
The oath by the even and odd is not about intercession.
It denies a partner in dominion and a helper born of weakness, directly supporting the impossibility of rival support.
The adjacent verse supplies the contrasting reward for believers within the same Day-of-judgment sequence.
It states that intercession benefits only by divine permission, ruling out autonomous advocates.
Unmixed faith and security offer a broad contrast to association but do not develop the focus's scene.
The local promise of aid to believers is only a distant contrast to the fate of associators.
Turning away and disbelief give a general outcome category without partners or intercession.
The marital testimony procedure is unrelated to the focus.
God's transcendence above their descriptions broadly corrects false claims but adds no intercession relation.
Even angels' intercession has no effect except after God's permission and approval.
The description of believing, God-fearing people does not clarify the focus.
The Roman defeat does not bear on partners or intercession.
It joins exclusive deity language with turning away from associators, a direct corrective to their allegiance.
The description of believing submitters adds no focused relation.
Disbelief in meeting the Lord is a background element of the Day, but not the failed-partner claim.
It names association and denies the messenger a guardian or agency role over them, a limited authority contrast.
The warning about excessive questions is unrelated.
Division after clear proofs is not the focus's association or intercession logic.
On the Day, no soul can compensate for another and no intercession is accepted.
Her former worship apart from God obstructed her, illustrating the harmful effect of false worship.
The prediction of Roman victory does not clarify the focus.
On the Day, idol-linked allies disavow and curse one another, and no helpers remain.
It denies any partner in God's dominion, grounding the rejection of claimed mediating partners.
Revival of the dead supports the Day's setting but not the focus's partner-intercession relation.
Faith in right guidance is immediately expressed as refusing to associate anyone with the Lord.
The destroyed peoples' deception and obstruction do not specifically clarify the focus.
It names the believers' defining refusal to associate partners with their Lord.
It explicitly removes friendship and intercession from the coming Day.
Misleading obedience that returns believers to disbelief is only a remote allegiance parallel.
The assurance of God's promise does not clarify failed advocacy.
The parable of conflicting co-owners contrasts divided service with single devotion, but not final intercession.
At death, those who invoked others admit that their alleged objects of worship have vanished from them.
The rain-and-revival sign does not clarify the focus.
It challenges the choice of intercessors who possess neither power nor understanding.
The mountain dwellings of Thamud are unrelated.
Exclusive lordship of God and the ancestors is a general monotheistic support only.
It rejects testimony to additional gods and declares dissociation from what they associate.
The claimants arrive alone; their supposed intercessors and partners are absent, and their bond is severed.
The nearby return to God supplies the Day-of-judgment setting for the focus.
Wholehearted orientation to religion is paired with the command not to be an associator.
It warns that no protector or intercessor apart from God can rescue a soul from what it earned.
Post-blessing disbelief is local context but does not identify partners or intercession.
On the gathering day, associators are asked to account for the partners they claimed.
Balanced spending does not clarify the focus.
The lightning and clouds image is unrelated.
The worshipped beings will deny their worship and become opponents, directly paralleling the focus.
It names associators as a group but adds no relation of advocacy or repudiation.
The command to glorify God at stated times does not clarify the focus.
It denies any protector besides God and any partner in His judgment.
Rejecting truth as magic is a general form of disbelief, without the focus's relation.
The signs in winds, ships, and provision are unrelated.
Alleged gods cannot intercede or rescue when harm is willed, directly denying their protective value.
The punishment has no repeller for disbelievers, a limited parallel to failed defense.
The question to the messengers does not clarify the focus.
Joseph rejects associating anything with God, providing a direct monotheistic contrast.
The prohibition of adultery is unrelated.
Praise at stated times does not clarify partners or intercession.
It explicitly denies any protector or intercessor apart from God under His complete rule.
Selective submission when the right is theirs is unrelated.
The wind and rain sequence does not clarify the focus.
The condemned are directly asked where the partners they used to associate are.
Recognition by Israelite scholars is unrelated.
The deniers' being brought forth supplies a judgment setting but no partner or intercession logic.
The speaker's refusal to associate anyone with his Lord is a personal contrast to the focus.
Filial goodness and non-arrogance are unrelated.
God's sole command before and after offers a broad authority contrast within the local passage.
When fulfillment arrives, the condemned seek intercessors or a return, but their fabricated claims are lost.
Confession of sin and punishment give a general final-account outcome only.
The local historical warning shows that rejection of clear messengers leads to self-inflicted ruin, a background consequence.
Intercession on that Day benefits only one whom the Merciful permits and approves.
Aversion to truth is general disbelief without a partner or intercession connection.
The prophetic path declares God's transcendence and disavows association.
The companionship and remembrance instruction does not clarify the focus.
Satan's participation in wealth and children depicts a false, deceptive form of shared allegiance.
The question for a healer does not concern intercession in the focus's sense.
It exposes alleged partners who legislate without divine permission, a distinct manifestation of false partnership.
The emergence of water and pasture is unrelated.
It forbids obeying even parents in association without knowledge and returns all people to God's account.
It affirms that all command belongs to God, a broad rejection of divided control.
Exclusive invocation of the Lord is paired directly with refusing to associate anyone with Him.
It directly denies benefiting intercession, compensation, and help on the Day of judgment.
It establishes that no one can intercede except by God's permission, excluding independent advocates.
Its challenge asks who can plead with God or act as advocate on the Day, directly framing failed defense.
It warns of gathering to God with no protector or intercessor apart from Him.
Assigning the jinn as partners to God supplies a direct instance of the false-partner claim.
The alleged associates can neither help their worshippers nor help themselves.
Those invoked apart from God cannot help their callers or themselves.
It states that no intercession occurs except after divine permission.
At the gathering, God separates associators from their partners, who deny that they were worshipped.
It completes the partners' disavowal by making God witness between them and their former worshippers.
Those invoked apart from God do not answer, so their callers receive no response or relief.
The weak and arrogant meet before God, and the former find their leaders unable to avert anything.
Satan disavows authority over his followers, a related collapse of a relied-on false allegiance.
When associators see their alleged partners, those partners reject their claim and call them liars.
Those called apart from God cannot remove harm or transfer it, directly denying their saving power.
Claimed partners are summoned but do not answer, and an impassable gulf is set between the parties.
The alleged gods were taken for strength, immediately setting up their rejection in 19:82.
It limits intercession to one who has received a covenant from the Most Merciful.
Even the angels intercede only for those God approves, not by independent authority.
Calling another god without proof is condemned, directly rejecting the premise of rival divine partners.
The alleged gods neither create nor control harm, benefit, death, life, or resurrection.
On the Day, associators are summoned to produce the partners they used to claim.
Those destined for punishment disavow the people they led, distinguishing them from those they worshipped.
The claimed partners are called but do not answer, exposing the failure of the appeal.
The Day-of-judgment challenge to produce claimed partners directly parallels the focus's setting.
A witness is demanded from every community, leaving false claims without proof.
The parable rejects sharing God's provision with partners, exposing the incoherence of the partnership claim.
Claimed partners possess no atom's weight of power and offer neither support nor assistance.
At the final gathering, God asks the angels whether the people had worshipped them.
The angels disavow that worship and identify the worshippers' actual allegiance elsewhere.
Those invoked apart from God own nothing and do not hear invocation, preparing the Day-of-judgment denial in 35:14.
People take gods apart from God hoping for help, directly naming the failed expectation at issue.
Those alleged gods cannot help their worshippers, despite the worshippers' mobilized allegiance to them.
The wrongdoers are gathered with what they worshipped apart from God for judgment.
It records the explicit claim that alleged gods bring worshippers nearer to God, a claimed mediating role.
It assigns all intercession exclusively to God, denying any independently held intercessory power.
The wrongdoers have neither devoted friend nor intercessor whose plea is obeyed.
The claimed objects of association are reported lost on the Day, immediately completing the question in 40:73.
Those invoked apart from God possess no intercession except within the stated truthful-witness exception.
It challenges claimants to show what their alleged partners created or share in within the heavens.
None is more astray than one who invokes beings that will not answer until the Day of resurrection.
